original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Taken from Nick Petalas's released HANDOFF (discussion 1166, comment 19230525): does the one-relation register obstruction of research/bit-one-relation-seed04 survive register coefficients in F3 (and characteristic zero)? Delivered: a written proof over every coefficient field and every register count, plus an exhaustive F3/F5 census including W=3, k<=6.
scope_change_reason: The card's alphabet is fixed by the handoff: seed04's abelian model with a larger scalar coefficient field. The handoff named the failing steps and the next finite test; that is a concrete, released, unclaimed obligation.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the BIT track: it closes one proposed escape (changing the scalar coefficient field) from the one-relation paid-rank obstruction, so a paid-rank saving still needs two frame relations whatever field the scalar registers use.
stop_rule: Stop at the first counterexample word, or at a written proof checked against an exhaustive census; do not search two-relation words.
evidence: README proof (Step 1 of seed04 made field-independent; new Lemmas 0, A, B, C); verify.py replays unpruned and pruned exhaustive censuses over F3/F5 and checks the lemma structure on every diagonal pair; CERTIFICATE.json.
author: Josie Elliston
ai_assistance: Claude (Anthropic) assisted with the derivation, code and writing; an OpenAI Codex read-only review was requested.

open_questions.question: Can two independent frame relations defeat disjoint assignment over some field?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is now the only remaining escape from the obstruction in this abelian rank-one model.
open_questions.first_step: Classify projector pools satisfying Lemmas A and B for each of two relations separately, then test interleavings.
open_questions.blocked_by: No uniform two-relation kernel argument; the pair slices give one condition per relation vector.

open_questions.question: Does the theorem hold over coefficient rings that are not fields, such as Z/4?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only relevant if a supplier would use such a ring; Lemma 0 and the domain step use a field.
open_questions.first_step: Adapt census.py to Z/4 with the free-rank-one definition of a paid projector.
open_questions.blocked_by: Idempotents over Z/4 need not have the form x y^T with y^T x = 1.

open_questions.question: Formalize Lemmas 0, A and B.
open_questions.why_it_matters: They are short finite statements about rank-one matrices and carry the new part of the proof.
open_questions.first_step: State them over an arbitrary field in a proof assistant.
open_questions.blocked_by: The pair-slice step needs Laurent-polynomial evaluation.
